I am 63 years old and have farmed these 35 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. I finished high school, so I read the extension pamphlets, check prices online, and talk to the seed dealer at the cooperative, but I always verify on my own fields before I trust anything new. My wife and I are the only ones living on the farm now, so I hire machinery services for ploughing, sowing, and harvest — I cannot afford to miss the sowing window trying to do everything by hand.

This year I am keeping 30 mu in my wheat-maize rotation and 5 mu in cotton. Our land is loamy alluvial soil with good depth. I paid for a soil test three years ago — it showed medium phosphorus but potassium getting low after so many years of wheat-maize, so I have been adjusting my formula every season since.

The winter wheat is already in the ground. I sowed Jimai 3266, an improved variety, last October on all 30 mu. I put down base fertilizer then, and now I am planning the spring topdress. I calculate 16 kg of nitrogen per mu total: about 40 kg of compound fertilizer at sowing and 20 kg of urea at jointing. I keep phosphorus at 6 kg per mu because the soil level is adequate, and potassium at 5 kg per mu. I will irrigate four times total — the overwinter water is done, and I will water at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Three pesticide sprays: one herbicide, one for aphids when they appear, and a fungicide at heading. I used rotary tillage before sowing. I am targeting 580 kg per mu, which is a bit better than last year’s 560 if we avoid a late frost.

For summer maize after wheat harvest, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid. I use no-tillage sowing to save time and catch the season — every day in June matters. I budget about 30 kg of compound fertilizer and 18 kg of urea per mu, giving 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium. Two irrigations are enough if I time them right: one at seedling stage and the absolutely critical one at tasseling-silking. Two pesticide applications, herbicide and one for corn borer. I expect 650 kg per mu.

For cotton on the 5 mu, I deep plough in April because cotton roots need loose soil down to 25 cm. I plant a Bt hybrid. Cotton takes more potassium than grain crops, so I apply about 40 kg of compound fertilizer plus 10 kg of potassium chloride per mu, giving 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium. I irrigate three times — at seedling establishment, flowering, and boll setting. Four pesticide sprays to control aphids and spider mites that the Bt does not stop. I expect 100 kg of lint cotton per mu, which is about 280 kg of seed cotton.

Fertilizer prices dropped about 10% from last year, so I am going back to my full rates. I learned 30 years ago that trying to save 100 yuan on fertilizer and losing 500 yuan in grain is a fool’s bargain. I watch what my neighbors apply, but my land is my responsibility, and I make the final numbers based on my own calculations.
